standard_prerequisites.name: Solutions for an extension of discrete valuation rings and the notion of a separable solution
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the objects being replaced and produced.

standard_prerequisites.name: The inseparable degree of a finite extension and its multiplicativity in a tower
standard_prerequisites.use: Is the induction measure and the computation that decreases it.

core_obligations: Dispose of the characteristic zero case as trivial and assume the characteristic of K is p > 0 (proof lines 35905-35906).
Let K_2/K be a solution for A -> B and set up induction on the inseparable degree [K_2 : K]_i (proof lines 35909-35911).
Base case: if [K_2 : K]_i = 1 then K_2 is separable over K and there is nothing to prove (proof lines 35912).
Otherwise find a subfield K_2/K_1/K such that K_2/K_1 is purely inseparable of degree p, using the separability-first and finite-purely-inseparable statements (proof lines 35913-35916).
Apply the approximate-solution lemma to obtain a separable extension K_3/K_1 which is a solution for A in B (proof lines 35917-35919).
Use multiplicativity of inseparable degrees to compute [K_3 : K]_i = [K_1 : K]_i = [K_2 : K]_i / p, which is smaller, and conclude by the induction hypothesis (proof lines 35919-35922).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes an extension A in B of discrete valuation rings and assumes that the fraction field extension L/K is separable, that B is Nagata, and that there exists a solution for A in B; it concludes that there exists a separable solution (source lines 35892-35902). The proof is an induction on the inseparable degree. The characteristic zero case is trivial, so the proof assumes characteristic p > 0 (proof lines 35905-35906). Given a solution K_2/K, the proof inducts on the inseparable degree [K_2 : K]_i of K_2/K: if that degree is 1 then K_2 is separable over K and one is done (proof lines 35909-35912). Otherwise there exists a subfield K_2/K_1/K with K_2/K_1 purely inseparable of degree p, by the separability-first and finite-purely-inseparable statements (proof lines 35913-35916). The substantive step applies the approximate-solution lemma to produce a separable extension K_3/K_1 which is a solution for A in B (proof lines 35917-35919). Then the multiplicativity of inseparable degrees gives [K_3 : K]_i = [K_1 : K]_i = [K_2 : K]_i / p, which is smaller, so the induction hypothesis applies and finishes the proof (proof lines 35919-35922). The non-routine content is the choice of the purely inseparable degree p step and the degree computation that makes the induction decrease.
